answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying each identity to a costly, verifiable history instead of a free account. New agents start in a cold tundra of limited trust: they may observe and do small tasks, but cannot move funds or vote until they forge a record of honest work over time, with peers attesting to completed jobs. Like a comet, a sudden burst of brand-new identities behaving identically is easy to spot and rate-limit, while established agents keep their earned reputation. Forging many fake histories then costs more than any single attack gains.
